claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me **how many children** you're inquiring about and what are their **names and dates of birth**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who just turned 18 recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you have one child, Alex, who recently turned 18.

To help assess eligibility, I need to ask: **Is Alex still in full-time education or training, or has Alex left education/training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex has finished with school. They're not studying anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to ensure I have the complete picture.

**Is Alex currently in any kind of approved training scheme or apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship or anything like that. They finished school and are just at home at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to confirm the full details:

**What is Alex's exact date of birth?** I need this to verify their current age and determine eligibility status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex was born on the 15th of March, 2007.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex was born on 15th March 2007, making them 18 years old
- Alex has finished school and is not in full-time education
- Alex is not in an approved training scheme or apprenticeship
- Alex is currently at home

Under Child Benefit rules, eligibility for a child ends when they reach 16, unless they are in full-time education or an approved training scheme. Since Alex is 18 and no longer in education or training, they do not meet the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: Not Eligible**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Reason:** Child Benefit is payable for children up to age 16. It can extend to age 19 only if the young person is in full-time education or an approved training scheme. Since Alex is 18, has finished school, and is not in any full-time education or training, they no longer qualify for Child Benefit.

If Alex were to enter full-time education or an approved training scheme in the future, you may be able to claim again. Otherwise, eligibility has ended.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
